title: Nitter has more working instances than before the takedowns
why_read: An interesting case study in resilience of decentralized/self-hosted mirror networks against platform takedown efforts.
analysis: Nitter is a privacy-friendly alternative front-end for Twitter/X, and this item reports that despite legal/technical takedown pressure, more instances are running than before crackdowns began. It's a mildly interesting story about the cat-and-mouse dynamics of open-source mirroring tools versus platform enforcement, though it's more of a community/political story than deep technical content. Engineers interested in scraping, API access, or self-hosting a resilient service architecture might find it moderately relevant.
